Subject: Request: Soft-landing downgrade protocol & one-time credit (Novamed)

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation, Novamed wants a clear downgrade / early termination path in the SOW so your product team can pilot with scaled expectations. You asked for a written proposal for the soft-landing terms we can offer (credits + ramp schedule + opt-out window) so procurement can sign off.

Proposed quick summary from our side (attached redline):
- One-time termination credit equal to 20% of committed MRR if Novamed elects early termination within the first 9 months.
- 90-day staged downgrade window: after notice, capacity steps down in 30-day increments with proportional credits and a guaranteed 7-day notice for autoscale reactivation.
- Opt-out language: customer may elect a one-time exit within the first 9 months with the credit above; subsequent downgrades follow standard downgrade policy.

Attachments: Novamed_SOW_v3.pdf, soft_landing_terms_redline.docx.

If those terms look reasonable I can escalate for a one-time exec approval (we typically need sign-off for anything outside the standard early termination schedule). Are you targeting legal sign-off this week?

Also copying Marissa and Karthik for visibility — Marissa, this will need an approval exception if we go above 15% credit or extend the opt-out beyond 6 months.

Next steps I propose: if Novamed confirms acceptance of the redline today, I’ll route to Deal Desk and request exec approval for the 20% credit and 90-day window.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Subject: EXTERNAL: Escalation — Novamed requests 30% early-term credit (exec approval request)

Marissa / Karthik —

Summary: Novamed (pilot opportunity) is asking for a one-time early termination credit of 30% if termination happens within the first 6 months (they'll accept 20% after month 6 up to month 9). They also want a guaranteed 48-hour burst re-enable SLA during the 90-day staged downgrade. Procurement wants written confirmation from us.

Why this matters: This is a strategically important pilot in the health vertical — potential expansion across 3 hospitals if pilot results are positive. They want stronger front-loaded protections because initial usage will be heavier on ingestion/QA. Standard policy allows up to 15% credit without exec sign-off; anything above that needs Deal Desk + VP sign-off.

Proposal for decision (recommendation):
- Approve a one-time 25% termination credit if termination is within 0–6 months (middle ground between 30% request and our standard 15%).
- Keep the 20% credit for terminations in months 6–9.
- Approve the 48-hour burst re-enable SLA for the pilot only, documented as a temporary operational window (not to be added to the master SLA).
- Require Novamed to sign the attached SOW redline and accept a 30-day operational review clause at month 2.

Operational notes:
- If approved, Deal Desk will record this as a one-time exception tied to deal_id RWD-2026-NOVA-487.
- Finance requests that the one-time credit be issued as service credit applied to final invoice rather than cash refund.

Can you confirm approval for the recommendation above or suggest modifications? They want written confirmation back to Procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Sean

Thanks for the clear recommendation and the context. I approve the proposed middle-ground exception with the following firm controls:

1) One-time termination credit: 25% if termination occurs within months 0–6. 20% for months 6–9. Credit to be issued as service credit on the final invoice; Finance will track under a one-off journal entry tagged to RWD-2026-NOVA-487.

2) 48-hour burst re-enable: Approved for the pilot period only. Add explicit operational guardrails: a) Novamed must provide 24-hour advance notice for non-emergency capacity increases when possible; b) Emergency calls for burst will be triaged and we will escalate to on-call infra within 2 hours with target re-enable within 48 hours. This is an operational commitment for the pilot and not a change to our standard SLA catalog.

3) Documentation & sign-off: Require Novamed to sign the redlined SOW and the one-off exception addendum. Once signed, Marissa (Deal Desk) will countersign and log the exception. Send the DocuSign link to Lydia; legal has pre-approved the addendum language.

4) Expiration: This exception is valid only for this deal and must be documented in HubSpot by Oct 15, 2026. No precedence to be implied for other deals.

Sean — please send a brief confirmation email to Lydia/procurement summarizing approved items and attach the DocuSign link. Mark the exception in the deal record and tag Finance.
